title: Fewest Terms
statement: A school offers n courses numbered 1 to n. Each rule [before, after] says one course must be passed in an earlier term than another. A student can take any number of courses in one term. Return the fewest terms to pass every course, or −1 if the rules make it impossible.

answerKey.pattern: Kahn's algorithm level by level: each level of the queue is one term
keyPoints: Start with every course that has no required course
Take a whole level per term; free the courses whose requirements are now all passed
If some course is never taken, the rules have a loop: −1
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Repeatedly scan all courses for ones that are ready: O(n · (n + m))

hints: Which courses can be taken in the first term?
Those with no required course. After that term, which become ready?
BFS by levels on Kahn's queue; count the levels; check that all n courses were taken.
